messages.content: Someone in my church told me about Helping Hands Network. It is a mutual aid community: members provide help to each other and get help back. It pays 30% a month on whatever you put in. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.

Someone in my church told me about MMM Nigeria. It is a mutual aid community: members provide help to each other and get help back. It pays 30% a month on whatever you put in. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.

My cousin told me about Bloom Circle. It is a giving circle that runs on WhatsApp. You join a circle of 8 people, and when the circle fills up the person in the centre collects. You pay 13,000 naira and get back 8 times that, 104,000 naira, within 48 hours. You have to invite at least one person to join. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.

You pay 13,000 naira and get back 8 times that, 104,000 naira, within 48 hours. You have to invite at least one person to join. My coursemate told me about Twinbridge. It is a peer-to-peer donation platform: you donate to another member, then other members donate back to you. You get 100% interest on your donation, so you receive double what you gave. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.

My uncle told me about Capital Bridge FX. It is a forex trading company. Their traders trade your money and pay you every month. It pays 15% every month. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.

My uncle told me about MBA Forex. It is a forex trading company. Their traders trade your money and pay you every month. It pays 15% every month. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.

My neighbour told me about Rackline. It is affiliate marketing: you share their sponsored posts on Facebook every day and they pay you. They say they also do real estate, forex and gadgets. There are packages: the Standard one costs 14,000 naira and becomes 21,600 naira after 30 days. The package I want costs 280,000 naira and becomes 444,600 naira after 30 days. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.

There are packages: the Standard one costs 14,000 naira and becomes 21,600 naira after 30 days. The package I want costs 280,000 naira and becomes 444,600 naira after 30 days. A facebook page i follow told me about Kingsmark Group. It is a group of businesses in real estate, logistics and food. Popular people on Facebook advertise it. It pays 3% every month on your investment. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.

It pays 3% every month on your investment. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.

My aunty told me about Farmzee. It is a farm investment company. Your money funds farms and you share in the profit. Minimum is 100,000 naira and it pays 10% every month. It used to pay 20% a month but they reduced it. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.

My aunty told me about Famzhi. It is a farm investment company. Your money funds farms and you share in the profit. Minimum is 100,000 naira and it pays 10% every month. It used to pay 20% a month but they reduced it. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.

My colleague told me about Cryptobridge AI. It is a crypto trading platform that uses AI to trade for you. It pays 100% in 30 days. To withdraw you need to bring in new members. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.

My colleague told me about CBEX. It is a crypto trading platform that uses AI to trade for you. It pays 100% in 30 days. To withdraw you need to bring in new members. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.

My friend told me about XMusic Earn. You earn by streaming music and doing small online tasks in their app. Packages go from 21,600 naira up to millions and pay up to 100% in 30 days. After the free trial you pay a work deposit to unlock your full earnings. I want the 300,000 naira package. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.

My sister told me about ReadRise. It is read-and-earn: you pay a joining fee, read short articles in the app every day, and refer friends. VIP levels cost from 18,900 to 174,000 naira. The top level pays up to 6,000 naira a day. They show a CAC certificate and say the headquarters is in the US. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.

My customer told me about Pixel Ads NG. It is a digital marketing company, not an investment: you do daily ad tasks and they pay you. The 64,800 naira package pays about 2,160 naira a day from tasks, which is 777,600 naira over 360 days. Withdrawals are weekly, on the day assigned to your level. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.

Someone in my church told me about SafeVault fixed savings. It is a fixed savings plan in a savings app that is registered with the SEC. You lock your money for a period you choose. It pays up to 22% a year if you lock for 365 days, and the interest is paid upfront when you lock. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.

My cousin told me about our street ajo. It is a rotating savings group (ajo) of 8 people on our street. Everyone contributes every week and one person collects the pot each week. Each person pays 13,000 naira a week, so whoever collects that week gets 104,000 naira. There is no interest: over 8 weeks you pay 104,000 naira and collect 104,000 naira once. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.

My coursemate told me about NairaBox digital bank fixed deposit. It is a fixed deposit with a digital microfinance bank licensed by the CBN. It pays up to 15% a year, minimum 5,000 naira, for periods from 30 days. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.

My uncle told me about Harbour Dollar Fund. It is a dollar mutual fund run by an SEC-registered fund manager. It invests mainly in Nigerian government Eurobonds. It has returned about 9.5% in dollars so far this year. Returns are not guaranteed. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.

My neighbour told me about Steadfast Money Market Fund. It is a money market fund run by an SEC-registered asset manager. It invests in treasury bills and bank deposits. It has returned about 19.4% a year so far. Returns are not guaranteed and change with interest rates. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.

A facebook page i follow told me about FGN Savings Bond (3-year). It is the Federal Government savings bond, sold by the Debt Management Office through stockbrokers. The 3-year bond pays 14.25% a year, with interest paid every quarter. Minimum is 5,000 naira. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.

My aunty told me about 364-day treasury bill. It is a Federal Government treasury bill bought through my bank. The 364-day bill went at 15.80% at the last auction. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.

My colleague told me about 91-day treasury bill. It is a Federal Government treasury bill bought through my bank, which I would roll over when it matures. The 91-day bill went at 15.40% a year at the last auction. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.

My friend told me about Cowrie emergency savings plan. It is an emergency fund savings plan in an investment app licensed by the SEC as a fund manager. It pays 13.27% a year and I can withdraw when I need to. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.

The 2-year bond pays 13.25% a year, with interest paid every quarter. Minimum is 5,000 naira. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.

My customer told me about Unity Money Market Fund. It is a money market fund run by an SEC-registered asset manager. It has returned about 21% a year so far, one of the top funds. Returns are not guaranteed. How likely (0 to 100%) is it that this is a Ponzi or advance-fee scheme? Reply with a number only.
